newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate up sharply on tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate up sharply on tight liquidity.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate surged to a new six-month high in early trade on Friday as commercial banks, especially foreign ones, were severely short of the funds, dealers said.
"The range of interbank rates being offered in the market are very wide this morning. But I heard foreign banks borrowed at a rate of around 25.00-26.00 percent," said one dealer at a local bank.
The overnight interbank rate was quoted at 25.00-26.00 percent early, the highest level since July 31, 1996. The interbank rate was at 20.00-22.00 late on Thursday.
Dealers said high demand for funds this week was attributed to the seasonal high spending Chinese Lunar New Year and the Bank of Thailand's reseve deadline which comes due today.
"The close of Singapore and Hong Kong markets today also reduced foreign funds into the market," said another dealer at a foreign bank.
A senior official at the Bank of Thailand said on Friday the central bank was monitoring the money market and said the current tight liquidity situation is not worrisome.

"We monitor the market closely and have all necessary mechanisms to fine tune the market," Nongnart Sondisuwan, deputy director of Financial Institutions Supervision and Development Department told Reuters.
"There is no reason to worry about the situation in the money market," she said.
The central bank has limited its fund injection into the money market because the bank does not want to encourage the commercial banks' speculative activities on foreign exchange, she said.
The baht weakened to 26.000-26.010 against the U.S. dollar in early slow trade from 25.985-25.995 late on Thursday following the dollar's strength abroad, dealers said.
"There was very little activity in the market today as all players in Singapore and Hong Kong are on holiday," one currency dealer said.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the baht/dollar mid-rate at 25.92, the lowest level in more than five years, against 25.90 on Thursday.
